source: human-verified pending: drafted by Claude from the code, to be reviewed by the owner

flaws.title: The /charge endpoint has no authentication
flaws.why: The /charge handler reads a card and amount and calls Charge with no check of who is calling, so anything that can reach the service can charge any card.

flaws.title: Payment gateway password is hardcoded in source
flaws.why: gatewayPassword is a string literal in the code, so everyone with repository access holds the payment gateway credential and it cannot be rotated without a deploy.

flaws.title: Full card number written to the log
flaws.why: log.Printf("charging card %s ...", card) puts the card number in plain text in every log line, which breaks PCI rules and leaks cards to anyone who reads logs.

flaws.title: A declined or failed charge is reported as success
flaws.why: Charge discards the response from http.Post and returns only err, which is nil for a 4xx or 5xx, so a declined card reads as charged; the response body is also never closed.

flaws.title: Payment gateway call has no timeout
flaws.why: http.Post uses the default client with no timeout, so a slow payment gateway holds every /charge request open without limit.

flaws.title: Charges take no idempotency key
flaws.why: Charge(card, amount) has no request id and sends none to the gateway, so a retried request charges the card again.

flaws.title: Amount is not validated
flaws.why: The amount from read(r) goes straight to Charge with no check for zero, negative or absurd values.

flaws.title: The gateway credential is never sent
flaws.why: gatewayPassword is declared but the http.Post call sends no credentials, so the payment gateway either rejects every charge or accepts unauthenticated ones.

flaws.title: Server has no timeouts and ignores its start error
flaws.why: http.ListenAndServe runs with no read or write timeouts (slow clients hold connections) and its returned error is dropped, so a failed bind exits silently.
